newsitem.title: ESTONIA: INTERVIEW - HANSAPANK TO DECIDE ON LITHUANIA IN H1 1997.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - HANSAPANK TO DECIDE ON LITHUANIA IN H1 1997.

text.p: Estonia's and the Baltics largest bank Hansapank is still considering a move into the Lithuanian market and expects to make a decision in the first half of this year, chairman Hannes Tamjarv said.
"Very clearly our next geographic step is to be operating in Lithuania," Tamjarv told Reuters in a recent interview.
"We are not making much public relations on the process but we are very seriously considering the alternatives," he added.
Hansapank has already said it will open a broker in Lithuania this year but expansion to banking in Lithuania will be in competition with other Estonian bank, Hoiupank .
"There is no rush, but clearly, in this year, we have to make a move," Tamjarv added.
"We will make our decision in the first half of 1997," Tamjarv said.
One of the reasons for expanding outside Estonia is that Hansapank was reaching the limits of its market share, he said.
"We clearly want to stay a selective high quality bank that means that we can hardly afford much more than 30 percent of the market. So clearly there is not much more to go," he said.

Hansapank is already present in Latvia with Hansabank-Latvija and Tamjarv said that from the financial point of view the move had not yet been successful although from an organisational view there was development.

"As we are trying to standardise the group's activities, it does not mean copying but still standardising the group's actitivities so we are trying to implement the same business idea in Hansabank-Latvija as for Hansapank Estonia," he said.
"We are choosing the best alternatives, so far pretty often the best alternatives come from Estonia," he added.
Tamjarv said that the state of the Estonian bank market was good although competition was strong.
"The market itself is in a pretty healthly shape, that is very clear and the trends are pretty healthly as well," he said.
"The competition is tightening but luckily enough it does not harm cooperation between the banks. We have a well-established banking association," he added.
He said there would be no big changes in the market although it was no secret merger talks have gone on and were going on.
"We have 14 banks and that sounds like six or seven too many," Tamjarv said.
He also said that Hoiupank was Hansapank's main competitor and was in fact a stronger competitor than the bank had imagined.
